prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right broker depends on your budget, health needs, whether you want ACA marketplace plans (with possible subsidies), HSAs, and how much hand‑holding you want. That said, here’s a practical way to find the best broker in Kansas City, MO, plus some reputable options and what to ask them.

Quick summary
- If you want local, in‑person help and someone familiar with Missouri’s ACA marketplace and small‑business/self‑employed issues, look for a licensed independent agent who is certified to enroll people on the federal marketplace (healthcare.gov).  
- Large regional brokerages with Kansas City offices (examples) include HUB International, Leavitt Group, and AssuredPartners — they handle individual and small‑business plans and have local presence. Online broker options (good for price shopping) include eHealth and other comparison sites.  
- Best approach: compare 2–3 brokers/agents, get multiple quotes, confirm marketplace certification, and choose the agent who explains subsidies, SEP rules, HSAs, and plan networks clearly.

Where to find and vet brokers
- Search the National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) “Find an Agent/Producer.”  
- Use healthcare.gov to find certified agents/navigators in Kansas City (Missouri uses the federal marketplace).  
- Check license status on the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance site (and Kansas DOI if you might enroll on the Kansas side).  
- Read local Google/Yelp reviews and BBB ratings.

Good local/regional names to consider (examples to check)
- HUB International — large regional broker with Kansas City office and full product range.  
- Leavitt Group — independent brokerage with a Kansas City presence and experience with small‑business/individual plans.  
- AssuredPartners — regional broker with Kansas City area offices.  
- Local independent agents you find through NAHU or healthcare.gov — sometimes smaller local agencies give more personalized service.

Questions to ask any broker/agent
- Are you licensed in Missouri (and Kansas, if relevant)? Are you certified to enroll people on the federal marketplace?  
- Do you work primarily with individual/sole‑proprietor clients or small businesses? How many similar clients do you handle?  
- Will you shop multiple carriers and provide a side‑by‑side comparison? Which carriers do you represent?  
- How are you paid — commissions only, or do you charge a broker fee? (Fee vs commission can matter for transparency.)  
- Do you know about SEP/qualifying life events and ACA subsidy eligibility for self‑employed people? Can you estimate premium tax credits?  
- Can you help with HSAs, dental/vision add‑ons, and provider/network verification?

Things to consider for self‑employed people
- Marketplace plans may qualify for premium tax credits based on household income; brokers experienced with ACA can estimate subsidies.  
- If you’re eligible for a High Deductible Health Plan (HDHP), confirm HSA compatibility and contribution limits.  
- If you want short‑term or association plans, make sure you understand limitations (preexisting conditions, out‑of‑pocket exposure).  
- Ask how the agent will help after enrollment (billing issues, renewals, claims assistance).

If you want, I can:
- Look up marketplace‑certified agents in Kansas City if you give your ZIP code; or  
- Get you side‑by‑side quotes for a sample household (age, family size, approximate income) so you can see plan and subsidy differences.

Which would you like to do next?
